title: Why @? The history of decorator syntax

kcs.statement: PEP 318 (Python 2.4) introduced @ decorators placed on the line before def, replacing the older pattern of writing f = staticmethod(f) after the function body.

problem_ideas: Rewrite a pre-2.4 class with f = classmethod(f) using @
List the readability problem with applying transforms after a long function body
Compare the rejected 'def f() [dec]:' form with @dec
Identify which Python version first allowed class decorators
Explain why @ was acceptable even though it was later used for matrix multiply
Match three rejected syntax proposals to their objections
